Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:10:1.english: And Israel was impoverished - Above it [in a preceding verse], it is written: "And they encamped against them and destroyed the produce of the land."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:11:1.hebrew: מחוזא - עיר שהיה רבא דר בתוכה, כך שמה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:11:1.english: Meḥoza - A city in which Rava lived; such is its name.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:11:2.english: Honor your wives - Honor your wives.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:12:1.hebrew: חתכו חוליות - תנור העשוי חוליות, מצרפו בכבשן כדרך כלי חרס, ואח"כ צירף החוליות ונתן חול בין חוליא לחוליא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:12:1.english: He cut it into segments - An oven made [of] segments: he fires it in a kiln in the manner of earthenware vessels, and afterwards he joined the segments together and placed sand between each segment.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:12:2.hebrew: ר"א מטהר - שאין זה כלי חרס, אלא בנין כעין כלי גללים וכלי אדמה שאין מקבלין טומאה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:12:2.english: Rabbi Eliezer deems [it] ritually pure - For this is not an earthenware vessel, but rather a structure, like vessels of dung and vessels of earth, which do not contract ritual impurity.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:12:3.hebrew: וחכמים מטמאין - דאזלי בתר חוליות. שאר תנורים שלהם היו עשוים כעין קדירות גדולות ופיו למעלה, וצורף בכבשן כשאר קדירות, ומטלטלים, אלא שהיה מושיבו על הארץ או על הדף, ומדביק את טפילות הטיט סביב על כולו לעשותו עב שיקלוט ויחזיק את חומו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:12:3.english: And the Sages deem [it] ritually impure - For they follow [the status of] the segments. Their other ovens were made like large pots with its opening on top, and [it was] fired in a kiln like other pots, and [they were] portable, except that one would set it on the ground or on a board, and plaster the coating of clay around all of it to make it thick so that it would absorb and retain its heat.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:1:1.hebrew: כדדרש רבא - דטובה מעשה של דוד ובת שבע משלהם, וספק אשת איש היא, שהיוצא למלחמת בית דוד גט כריתות כותב לאשתו על מנת שאם ימות שתהא מגורשת מעכשיו, ולא תיזקק ליבם. וכל אותן הימים היא ספק מגורשת: אם מת, מגורשת מתחילה, ואם לא מת, לא נתגרשה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:1:1.english: As Rava expounded - For the deed of David and Bathsheba was better than theirs [those who humiliate others], and she was [a woman of] uncertain married status, for anyone who went out to the war of the House of David would write a bill of divorce for his wife on condition that if he dies, she shall be divorced from now, and she would not be bound to a levir [deceased husband's brother]. And all those days she is of uncertain divorce status: if he died, she was divorced from the beginning, and if he did not die, she was not divorced.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:1:2.hebrew: ובצלעי - בשביל אשתי זו שמתחילה חטאתי בה, כמו (בראשית ב) ויבן את הצלע: שמחו ונאספו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:1:2.english: And in my limping - [That is,] because of this wife of mine with whom I sinned initially, as [it says] (Genesis 2): "And He built the rib." They rejoiced and gathered:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:1:3.english: They tore and did not bleed - If they tore me, they would not find blood.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:3:1.hebrew: היא מוצאת והיא שלחה - אע"פ שהיו מוציאין אותה לשריפה, לא אמרה להם "ליהודה נבעלתי", אלא שלחה לו "למי שאלה לו אנכי הרה", ואם יודה הוא — מעצמו יודה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:3:1.english: She was brought forth, and she sent - Even though they were taking her out to be burned, she did not say to them, "I had relations with Judah"; rather, she sent to him, "By the one to whom these belong, I am pregnant," and if he confesses, he will confess on his own.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:4:1.english: His colleague [amito] - [A contraction of] am ito [a people with him].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:4:2.english: Regarding mistreatment of his wife - [Meaning] verbal mistreatment, to cause her distress.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:4:3.hebrew: אונאתה קרובה - לבא, פורענות אונאתה ממהר לבא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:4:3.english: Her mistreatment is near - [To] come; the punishment for mistreating her hastens to come.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:5:1.hebrew: שמעה תפלתי - אין לשנותו מלשון בקשה, שמבקש מאת הקב"ה שישמע תפלתו; אבל "אל תחרש" יש לשנותו מלשון בקשה, ולומר: בזו אני בוטח, שאין דרכך לשתוק ולא להחריש. "אל תחרש", "אל תעשה", "אל תתן" — משמשין לשון בקשה ומשמשין לשון עתיד, כגון (תהלים קכא) "אל יתן למוט" — הרי לשון בקשה; "ויאמר יעקב לא תתן לי מאומה" (בראשית ל) — הוא לשון עתיד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:5:1.english: Hear my prayer - One cannot change it from an expression of entreaty, for he is entreating the Holy One, blessed be He, to hear his prayer. However, “keep not silence” (“al techerash”) can be changed from an expression of entreaty, to say: “In this I trust, that it is not Your way to be quiet nor to remain silent.” [Expressions such as] “al techerash” [“be not silent”], “al ta'aseh” [“do not do”], [and] “al titten” [“do not give”] serve [both as] an expression of entreaty and as an expression of the future [tense]. For example, “May He not allow [your foot] to slip” (Psalms 121:3) — behold, [that is] an expression of entreaty; “And Jacob said, ‘You shall not give me anything’” (Genesis 30:31) — [that] is an expression of the future [tense].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:6:1.english: But there was none like Ahab - [The] end of the verse [is]: "whom Jezebel his wife incited."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:6:2.hebrew: [אתתך גוצא - אשתך קטנה, כפוף עצמך ושמע דבריה]:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:6:2.english: Your wife is short - [If] your wife is short, bend down and listen to her words.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:7:1.english: All the gates - of prayer are locked.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:7:2.hebrew: חוץ משערי אונאה - הצועק על אונאת דברים, אין השער ננעל בפניו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:7:2.english: Except for the gates of mistreatment - [For] one who cries out over verbal mistreatment, the gate is not locked before him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:7:3.hebrew: הכל ע"י שליח - נפרעים על כל עבירות ע"י שליח:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:7:3.english: Everything [is punished] by means of an agent - Retribution is exacted for all transgressions by means of an agent.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:7:4.english: And in His hand - He did not hand it over to an agent.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:8:1.english: Curtain - A partition that [is] between the Divine Presence and the heavenly host.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:8:2.hebrew: אינו ננעל - להפסיד ראייתן מן המקום, אלא תמיד רואה אותם עד שיפרע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:8:2.english: Is not locked - To block the sight of them from the Omnipresent; rather, He continually sees them until He exacts punishment.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:8:3.english: And in His hand [is] a plumb line - [This] implies that it is always with Him and He uses it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:8:4.hebrew: על פני - לפני, ואין מחיצה בינו לבין העבירה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:8:4.english: Before Me - Before Me, and there is no partition between Him and the transgression.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:9:1.english: When [is] your border peace - When the Holy One, blessed be He, satisfies you with the finest wheat.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:9:2.english: From the jug - A jug in which they place barley.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:9:3.hebrew: נקיש ואתי תגרא - התגר מקשקש ובא. ואני שמעתי: הכד מקשקש כדרך כלי ריקם שנשמע בו קול הברה כשמקשקשין עליו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 59a:9:3.english: Quarrel knocks and comes - Quarrel knocks and comes. And I heard [another explanation]: the jug rattles, in the manner of an empty vessel in which a reverberating sound is heard when one knocks upon it.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59a:12:1.hebrew: חתכו חוליות ונתן חול בין חוליא לחוליא - אם לא היה חול בינתים, היה מודה רבי אליעזר דכלי חשוב הוא, שהטפלה סביב לתנור מחברת החוליות ומעמידתן זו אצל זו; ומשום דנתן חול בינתים להפריד החוליות זו מזו, מטהר ר"א. והכי תנן במסכת כלים (פרק ה משנה ח): "חתכו לרוחבו פחות פחות מארבעה טפחים — טהור; מרחו בטיט — טמא משיסיקנו לאפות בו סופגנים. הרחיק את הטפלה ונתן חול או צרור בינתים — בזה אמרו: הנדה והטמאה והטהורה אופות בו, והוא טהור." קתני חול דומיא דצרור, שהוא יבש:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59a:12:1.english: "If one cut it into segments and placed sand between each segment" - If there had not been sand between them, Rabbi Eliezer would have agreed that it is a significant [complete] vessel, because the plastering around the oven connects the segments and holds them together next to one another; and because he placed sand between them to separate the segments from one another, Rabbi Eliezer deems it pure. And thus we learned in a Mishnah in tractate Kelim (chapter 5, mishnah 8): "If one cut it widthwise [into segments] each less than four handbreadths, it is pure; if one smeared it with clay, it becomes susceptible to impurity once one heats it [enough] to bake sponge cakes in it. If one distanced the plastering and placed sand or a pebble between them — concerning this they said: a menstruant, an impure woman, and a pure woman may bake in it, and it remains pure." It teaches "sand" [as] similar to "a pebble," which is dry.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59a:1:1.hebrew: נוח לו לאדם שיבא על ספק אשת איש כו' - נקט הכי משום דבת שבע ספק אשת איש הויא, ופי' בקונטרס משום דכל היוצא למלחמת בית דוד כותב גט לאשתו ע"מ שאם ימות יגרשנה ולא תיזקק ליבם, וכל אותם הימים היא ספק מגורשת. וק' לר"ת: דא"כ אין זה "כל היוצא", אלא דוקא שיש להם אחין ואין להם בנים. מיהו בקונטרס לאו דוקא נקט יבם, אלא שלא תתעגן. ועוד קשה לר"ת: דאמר במסכת שבת (ד' נו. ושם ד"ה גט): "כל האומר דוד חטא אינו אלא טועה" — אמאי? והא חזר אוריה מן המלחמה אח"כ! ומיהו יש לדחות שהיו מתנין אם לא יחזור בסוף המלחמה. ועוד קשה: דתניא בפ' מי שאחזו (גיטין דף עג. ושם: ד"ה אמר): "מה היא באותן הימים? רבי יהודה אומר: הרי היא כאשת איש לכל דבריה; ר' יוסי אומר: מגורשת ואינה מגורשת." ואפילו לרבי יוסי חטא דוד, דאינה מגורשת ודאי. וכ"ת דהתם בלא אמר "מעכשיו", דמוקי לה בגמרא באומר "מעת שאני בעולם", כלומר שעה אחת קודם מיתתי, ובמלחמת [בית] דוד היו כותבים "מהיום" — הא קתני בהדיא בתוספתא: "מהיום אם מתי, הימים שבינתים, רבי יהודה אומר: היא כאשת איש". ומתני' דמי שאחזו (שם) נמי מוכח דאמר "מהיום", דאדלעיל מיניה קאי. והא דאמר בגמרא באומר "מעת שאני בעולם", מפ' ר"ת ור"ח דפירושו: נעשה כאומר "מעת שהוא בעולם", משום כיון דאמר "אם מתי", מתכוין לרחק הגרושין כמו שיוכל ואינו רוצה שתתגרש עד סמוך למיתתו; והא דקאמר "מהיום", להראות שהוא רוצה שיחולו גרושין (. מהיום). ומפ' ר"ת: דבמלחמת בית דוד היו מגרשין לגמרי בלא שום תנאי, אלא היו עושין הדבר בצנעה כדי שלא יהו קופצין על נשותיהן לנושאן; לכך קרו להו "ספק אשת איש". ולכל הפי' קשה: דאפילו בא על אשת איש ודאי טוב ממלבין, מדקאמר דוד: "הבא על אשת איש מיתתו בחנק ויש לו חלק לעולם הבא, אבל מלבין כו'":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59a:1:1.english: It is preferable for a person to engage in intercourse with a woman whose married status is uncertain, etc. - [The Gemara] stated it this way because Bathsheba was of uncertain married status. And Rashi explained [that this was] because everyone who went out to war for the House of David would write a bill of divorce for his wife on condition that if he died, it would divorce her so that she would not be bound to a levir (yavam), and during all those days she was doubtfully divorced. And Rabbeinu Tam finds this difficult: if so, this would not [apply to] "everyone who went out," but only to those who have brothers and have no children. However, Rashi did not mean a levir specifically, but rather so that she would not become an agunah [a woman chained to a marriage]. And Rabbeinu Tam has a further difficulty: for [the Gemara] says in Tractate Shabbat (56a, and there s.v. Get): "Anyone who says David sinned is merely mistaken." Why [would he not have sinned]? Uriah returned from the war afterward! However, one can deflect [this difficulty by saying] that they would stipulate [that the divorce take effect] if he does not return at the end of the war. And there is a further difficulty: for it is taught in a baraita in the chapter Mi She'achazo (Gittin 73a, and there [73b] s.v. Amar): "What is her status during those days? Rabbi Yehuda says: She is like a married woman in all respects; Rabbi Yosei says: She is divorced and not divorced." And even according to Rabbi Yosei, David sinned, since she is not certainly divorced. And if you should say that there [in Gittin, the baraita speaks of a case] where he did not say "from now," as the Gemara establishes it [as referring] to one who says "from the time that I am in the world," meaning one hour before my death, whereas in the war of the [House of] David they would write "from today" — surely it is taught explicitly in the Tosefta: "[If he said] 'from today if I die,' [regarding] the days in between, Rabbi Yehuda says: She is a married woman." And the Mishnah in Mi She'achazo (ibid.) also proves that he said "from today," because it refers back to the preceding [Mishnah]. And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says, "when he says 'from the time that I am in the world,'" Rabbeinu Tam and Rabbeinu Chananel explain that its meaning is: he is treated as one who says "from the time that he is in the world," because since he said "if I die," he intends to distance the divorce as much as he can and does not want her to be divorced until close to his death; and that which he said "from today" [was only] to show that he wants the divorce to take effect (from today). And Rabbeinu Tam explains that in the war of the House of David, they would divorce [their wives] completely without any condition, except that they would do the matter in private so that [other men] would not jump at [the opportunity to marry] their wives; therefore they called them "of uncertain married status." And according to all the explanations, it is difficult: for even one who engages in intercourse with a woman who is certainly married is better off than one who humiliates [another], since David says: "One who engages in intercourse with a married woman, his death is by strangulation and he has a share in the World-to-Come, whereas one who humiliates, etc.":

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59a:2:1.hebrew: ולא עוד אלא בשעה שעוסקין בנגעים ואהלות - כלומר: לא מבעיא בשעה שהם בטלים, אלא אפי' עסוקים בהלכות חמורות, וגם אין עניינם לאשת איש. ויש ספרים דגרסי: "בשעה שעוסקין בארבע מיתות ב"ד":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59a:2:1.english: "And moreover, [even] at the time when they are engaged in [the laws of] Nega'im and Ohalot" - That is to say: it is unnecessary [to state] at a time when they are idle, rather even [when] they are engaged in weighty laws, and furthermore their subject matter has no [connection] to a married woman. And there are texts that read: "at the time when they are engaged in [the laws of] the four death penalties of the court."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59a:3:1.hebrew: דכתיב היא מוצת - בלא אל"ף, כמו (איכה ד׳:י״א): "ויצת אש בציון", שהיתה קרובה לאש כבר, ולא שלחה לו אלא ברמז; אם לא היה מודה, לא היתה מפרסמתו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59a:3:1.english: As it is written: "Hi mutzat" - Without an alef, like (Lamentations 4:11): "He kindled [vayatzet] a fire in Zion," for she was already close to the fire, and she sent [word] to him only by way of a hint; if he had not confessed, she would not have exposed him.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59a:5:1.hebrew: ואל דמעתי אל תחרש - אינו אומר "שמע אל בכיי" או "ראה דמעתי", אלא "אל תחרש"; כלומר, בטוח אני שלא תחרש, דשערי דמעות לא ננעלו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 59a:5:1.english: And "at my tears, keep not silence" - It does not say "hear my weeping" or "see my tears," rather "keep not silence" — that is to say, I am confident that You will not keep silent, for the gates of tears were not locked.
